itens.trecho: "Adèle" (Adèle Exarchopoulos) is a bit of a fish out of water at school. She doesn't quite fit in and finds the whole "boy" thing a bit of a turn off. Luckily the school also has it's extrovert in the blue-haired "Emma" (Léa Seydoux).

Too much footage and too little substance This three-hour movie is, at the very least, an hour and a half too long. It is riddled with superfluous scenes that add nothing to the plot and only serve as filler. It is a shame, because the central story of love and heartbreak is beautiful and features great performances by its two protagonists.

I became obsessed with Adele Exarchopoulos after seeing this. Didn't even have to look up that spelling. I ordered a custom-made 32" x 48" ish sized poster of her for my apartment that's still around somewhere. I'm pretty sure I tried to find her on snapchat. Thanks for reading.
